record.what_it_does: Issue tracking and project management for software teams, with cycles, projects and roadmaps.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code (PKCE supported) with user or app actor. Client credentials for app actors. Personal API keys are sent as a raw Authorization header. Access tokens last 24h and refresh tokens 30 days.
record.access_notes: The OAuth docs mention no app review. Any workspace admin can create an OAuth app and API keys. I did not check whether the free plan limits API use, and the docs did not say. Creating or reading webhooks needs workspace admin access or the admin scope.
record.api_breadth_notes: A single GraphQL API at api.linear.app/graphql that is also used internally. It covers issues, projects, cycles, comments, documents, customers, initiatives, teams and users. The schema supports introspection and there is a TypeScript SDK. I did not count operations.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (read-write) and https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly. OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, or a Bearer token or API key.
record.blocker_notes: There is no review gate. The API is GraphQL only, so there is no OpenAPI spec. Linear has no dedicated sandbox, but a free workspace can serve as a test environment.

evidence.quote: Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance.
It supports introspection so you can query the whole schema.
Only workspace admins, or OAuth applications with the `admin` scope, can create or read webhooks.
Read-write access is provided through `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp` by default.

record.needs_human: Check whether Linear's free plan restricts API or OAuth app creation, and whether there are rate limits. I did not open the pricing page. The OAuth page was silent on app review, so I inferred there is none.
